summary:
Lunar Mission is a zero-dependency, pixel-art 2.5D lunar sample-return simulator that turns NASA space mission design into cooperative gameplay for up to four players (via Crew Lobby, AI squadmates, local co-op, or multi-tab sync) with customizable astronaut avatars across the Launch, Space, Science, and Ground segments.

Players begin with Pre-Phase A formulation, selecting a lunar science objective, launch vehicle, and budget, before entering an Overcooked-style assembly hangar to fabricate payloads like spectrometers, solar-batteries, Ka-band relays, and descent cryo-stages against Concept Maturity Level (CML) requirements. Every engineering choice ripples across four playable stages: rocket ascent and Max-Q booster staging; Among Us-style cruiser crisis management during eclipses and surges; powered lunar landing, dual-rover 2.5D cliff EVAs, and core drilling; and lunar ascent, Earth skip-reentry, and carrier recovery. A Stage 5 Black Box Flight Recorder then links every early trade-off to final survival and science yield.

By gamifying mass, power, cost, communications, and risk margins in real time, Lunar Mission makes complex aerospace systems engineering intuitive, collaborative, and memorable.
details:
Lunar Mission is a zero-dependency, pixel-art 2.5D lunar sample-return simulator playable online on Render.com. One to four players design, manage, and fly a complete space mission from concept to splashdown across four NASA roles: P1 Launch, P2 Space, P3 Science, and P4 Ground.

• Pre-Game Flow (Title -> Crew Lobby -> Mission Setup): Players start from a pixel-art attract screen and enter a 4-seat Crew Lobby with customizable astronaut avatars (skin tone, hair, helmet, and mission badges) and deterministic AI bot backfill. Teams can play Solo Hot-Swap (keys 1-4), 4P AI Squad (with BFS pathfinding), Local 2P Co-Op (WASD + IJKL), Cross-Tab 4P (BroadcastChannel), or Online 4P Co-Op through the built-in WebSocket relay. In Mission Setup, players pick a Science Objective, Scenario/Difficulty (including Open Sandbox), and Launch Vehicle while tracking NASA Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1-4).

• Stage 1A (Assembly Hangar): In an Overcooked-style assembly hangar, crewmates process raw parts on Weld, Calibrate, and Charge benches, plate them onto Fairing Trays, and ship spacecraft modules (Lunar Spectrometer, Rover Solar-Battery, Deep-Space Ka-Relay, and Descent Cryo-Stage) while balancing live Mass, Power, Budget, Comms, and Fuel margins.

• Stage 1B (Rocket Liftoff & Ascent): Players hold vertical thrust and horizontal pitch inside the flight corridor against wind shear gusts, then decouple the booster during the Max-Q staging window.

• Stage 2 (Orbital Mission Control): Crewmates roam a 5-bay cruiser deck to clear console mini-games (Spectrometer Target Tracking, Eclipse Load-Shedding Breakers, Ka-Band Wave Alignment, and Wrench Bolt Torque), execute an MCC-1 trajectory burn, and override bulkheads locked by solar flares or micrometeoroid surges.

• Stage 3 (3A-3C Lunar Descent, Dual Rover EVA & Moon Launch): Crewmates land under retro-thrust at Point A, drive two 6-wheeled rovers (LTV-1 and LTV-2) across 2.5D lunar cliffs using ramps and RCS hops, complete 3 surface EVA tasks, drill core samples at Point B Crater, and launch into a timed Trans-Earth Injection (TEI) burn.

• Stage 4 & Stage 5 (Skip-Reentry, Recovery & Black Box Debrief): The crew holds the Earth atmospheric entry corridor, rolls to shed heat, vents cryo coolant, deploys Triple Main Chutes in the 8-18 km altitude window, and steers onto the recovery carrier. Stage 5 grades the run across four NASA pillars (S/A/B/C), plots an interactive telemetry replay timeline, and logs every decision in a causal Black Box Flight Recorder.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Every Stage 1 hardware choice and mid-mission dilemma carries downstream consequences across the flight: overweight builds burn extra ascent fuel and drop faster during lunar landing, Solar-Batteries prevent Stage 2 eclipse brownouts and extend rover range, and Ka-Relays widen the Stage 4 reentry corridor. Because the game runs on Render.com in any modern browser with zero installation, students, educators, and teams can jump into a shared room code immediately.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

• Core Web Stack (Zero Dependencies): HTML5 Canvas (560x310 pixel-art renderer scaled nearest-neighbor to a 1120x620 devicePixelRatio-aware viewport), CSS3 (notched 2px pixel-frame UI), and native browser ES Modules (JavaScript) with no npm packages or bundlers.

• Multiplayer & Hosting: Deployed on Render.com using our zero-dependency Node.js WebSocket relay and static server (relay-server.mjs over HTTPS/WSS), alongside BroadcastChannel for cross-tab sync, Web Audio API for procedural SFX, LocalStorage for crew profiles and run history, and a local Python/Node server option.

• Art & Audio Pipeline: Custom pixel art, layered backgrounds, animated benches, and spacecraft/explosion sprites authored in PNG sheets, plus an original soundtrack composed in FL Studio (.flp) and custom foley SFX.

Creativity

Lunar Mission combines Overcooked-style payload assembly, Among Us-style shipboard repair, 2.5D lunar rover driving, and orbital/reentry flight control into one continuous NASA mission loop. The modules you bolt together in Stage 1 become the exact hardware keeping your crew and cryogenic samples alive on the way back to Earth.

Factors Considered by the Team

• Accessibility & Onboarding: We built an interactive Corner UI Spotlight Tour, hangar walkthrough, Active Target Recipe Bar, live blueprint drawer (B), and mid-mission dilemma modals so new players learn systems engineering trade-offs as they play.

• Multi-Resource Engineering Trades: Mass, power, budget, fuel, communications downlink, and space weather hazards pull against each other, forcing crews to balance margins rather than follow a single optimal build.

• Flexible Play Modes: One to four players can run the mission solo, with an AI squad, in local 2P co-op, across browser tabs, or online via WebSocket room codes.
